Its start page offers two versions, Classic and Plus, a fan-made extension of the original. It supports keyboard and touch. Mini DayZ is a pixel-art survival game from Bohemia Interactive, the studio behind DayZ, that began as a fan-made browser game and came to mobile in 2017. In a randomly generated world you scavenge villages and cities for supplies while zombies, rabid dogs and bandits hunt you.

title: Homeworld
author: Gardens of Kadesh
description: Homeworld, from Gardens of Kadesh, runs the 1999 space strategy game in the browser as a WebAssembly build made with Emscripten and rendered with WebGL, with nothing to install. It is the web version of the Gardens of Kadesh project, a fan-maintained update of Homeworld that grew out of the earlier Homeworld SDL port, and the page opens on its version 1.2.2 title menu with Training, Single Player, Multiplayer, Options and Credits. Homeworld is a 1999 3D real-time strategy game from Relic Entertainment, published by Sierra, in which you command the fleet of exiled Kushan survivors across space in fully three-dimensional battles.

title: Fallout Nevada
author: roginvs
description: Fallout Nevada, from roginvs, plays the Fallout 2 total conversion Fallout: Nevada in the browser through a WebAssembly build of the Fallout 2 CE engine, with nothing to install. The page offers the English version of the mod, with ten save slots that live in your browser and a hi-res mode you can switch on or off, and it can download the game for offline play or clear its cache. The tilde key works as Escape, a two-finger tap acts as a right click, and F11 or Ctrl+F goes fullscreen. The same site also hosts Fallout: Sonora, and it has a Russian page as well. Fallout: Nevada is a total conversion of Fallout 2 by the Russian team Nevada Band, with a story of its own set before the first Fallout, following the vault that later became Vault City. It brings more than 100 quests, a new world map and new music, and its last build came out in 2015.

title: Cut the Rope DX
author: yell0wsuit
description: Cut the Rope DX, from yell0wsuit, is an enhanced version of the PC Cut the Rope that runs in the browser as a WebAssembly build rendered with Skia, with nothing to install. Once it has loaded it can be installed as an app and works offline, and your progress is saved in your browser. Drag across a rope or click it to cut it, as you prefer in the options, then guide the candy to Om Nom and collect the stars on the way. On top of the original it adds more box themes, such as the Spooky Box and the Mechanical Box, a Christmas theme in December and January, bug fixes, a level editor and a choice of languages. It supports keyboard and touch. Cut the Rope is a 2010 physics puzzle game from ZeptoLab, first released for iOS, in which you cut ropes to feed candy to the hungry Om Nom.

title: DBZ: Budokai 2
author: zero10
description: Note: Long initial load. Dragon Ball Z: Budokai 2 Web Online, from zero10, plays the PlayStation 2 fighting game in the browser with WebAssembly and WebGPU, with nothing to install. The page streams the game data as it needs it, runs at 60 FPS and has an Online tab in its settings. On a keyboard, W or Space confirms, X cancels, the arrow keys move and Enter starts, and controllers work as soon as they are plugged in. The control bar offers fullscreen, save and load states, settings, mute and restart. The settings let you set the sound volume, choose 60 or 30 FPS and pick the original 4:3 picture or 16:9 widescreen; they are remembered in your browser, and switching the frame rate reloads the engine. Dragon Ball Z: Budokai 2 is a 2003 fighting game for the PlayStation 2 and GameCube from Dimps, based on the Dragon Ball Z anime.

title: MU Online
author: muclaude.online
description: Note: Site and menu interfaces are in Portuguese. Mu Claude, at muclaude.online, is MU Online Season 6 ported to the browser with REA and WebAssembly. The site and the in-game menus are in Portuguese, although some event messages appear in English. The start screen has Menu and Credit buttons, with sound, fullscreen, keyboard help and Discord buttons down the side, and you begin in Lorencia with the classic interface, merchants and an inventory screen, while events such as Happy Hour are announced in the chat. A menu opens with a season pass, rewards, events, rankings, support, an auction house, a jewel bank, news, your account and voting. The season pass has 30 tiers on two tracks: a free track for everyone and a premium track that costs 1,000 WCoin, which makes it the paid part of the game, although the screens do not say how WCoin is obtained. The rewards include Zen, jewels such as Bless, Soul, Chaos and Life, Boxes of Kundun and gemstones, and claiming them needs a character at level 100 or with one reset. MU Online is a 2001 fantasy online role-playing game from Webzen, and Season 6 is one of its later content updates.

title: Carrion
author: AgentCube
description: Note: Music has been disabled to improve performance. This is a WebAssembly build of Carrion by AgentCube. The page loads about 600 files before the game starts, shows a frame rate counter, and has the music turned off for smoother performance. It is played with the keyboard. Carrion is a 2020 reverse-horror game from Phobia Game Studio in which you play a shapeless red creature that escapes from a facility and hunts the humans who held it.

title: NFS: Most Wanted
author: dezm0n
description: This is dezm0n's unofficial, experimental browser port of Need for Speed: Most Wanted, which is still in development. It is based on earlier work by austynoconnor and runs in the browser with WebAssembly and WebGPU. The game files load automatically as they are needed and stay cached in your browser. On a keyboard, Enter confirms and Esc goes back; on a controller, A or the cross button confirms and B or the circle button goes back, and you press a button after connecting the controller. Controls can be remapped under Options, then Controls, and the changes are saved to your player profile. It has Rockport, the Blacklist, police pursuits and the BMW M3 GTR, and manual saves and autosave are kept in your browser, with Files and saves, then Manage, for exporting and importing saves. Video settings are remembered, and the defaults are maximum graphics at 1920x1080. Performance depends on your processor and graphics card, online and LAN modes are not supported, and full-career driving and autosave at the end of a race still need testing. The game and its pages are in English only. The page says it is not affiliated with the original publishers. Need for Speed: Most Wanted is a 2005 street racing game from EA Black Box and Electronic Arts, in which you take on the Blacklist rivals and evade police pursuits across the city of Rockport.

title: WoW Classic
author: keldurn
description: Keldurn is a browser-played classic fantasy world from keldurn, listed here as WoW Classic. The site presents it as "a classic world. A new adventure.". It is played entirely in the browser, with nothing to install and no game-server port to expose. You sign in with a Keldurn account, or with Google or Discord, and Keldurn then prepares your private game credentials automatically. The site is available in English and Spanish. Its terms ask for one account per person unless the operator approves otherwise, and ask players not to automate play, trade accounts or currency, or exploit defects. World of Warcraft Classic is Blizzard's 2019 re-release of the original 2004 World of Warcraft online role-playing game.

title: Kerbal Space Program
author: crackers
description: Note: Very long initial load. This browser version of Kerbal Space Program 1.12.5 is credited to crackers. The page opens in CKAN, the mod manager for the game, with a Play button on its toolbar to launch Kerbal Space Program. Its mod list offers eight mods that are available to download rather than already installed: BackgroundThrust, BetterTimeWarp, EVE, KerbalEngineer, kOS, MechJeb2, Trajectories and ZTheme. The first load takes a very long time, and the game is played with the keyboard. Kerbal Space Program is a space flight simulation game from Squad in which you build rockets, planes and spacecraft out of parts and fly them to planets and moons around the Kerbol system, running a space program staffed by small green Kerbals.

title: Crimsonland
author: banteg
description: Crimsonland by banteg is a fan project that brings the 2003 shooter back to the browser. The original game was reverse engineered into C/C++ source that compiles to the same machine code as the original executable, and that code is what runs in your browser, so the weapons, perks and quests play like the original. The original art and sound are used with permission from 10tons. On top of that it supports modern gamepads and has an online leaderboard: tick Ranked in the Play Game menu and play Survival or a quest to the end, and the game uploads your run with a recording that the server plays back to check the score. Survival is ranked by experience and quests by time, with a separate hardcore board, and bots are welcome on their own entries. There is a co-op option, your saves are kept in your browser, and you do not need to sign up, because the game makes a keypair on first launch that acts as your account. On a phone, Crimsonland plays with a connected gamepad. The site says it is not affiliated with 10tons. Crimsonland is a 2003 top-down shooter from 10tons in which you survive hordes of creatures, picking perks as you level up and using a wide range of weapons.

title: Link's Arena
author: aperezpaya
file_requirement_review: {"title": "Link's Arena", "detail_url": "https://ported2browser.com/ports/01M553P1891NC0ZPZ3EJ8N9TAJ", "direct_url": "https://linksarena.pages.dev/", "basis": "directory_about_review", "required": false, "optional": true, "disc_image": false, "scope": "alternative", "note": "Links Arena admite ROM propia como alternativa a recursos alojados tras declarar posesion."}
description: Link's Arena by aperezpaya is an unofficial, fan-made multiplayer mod of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time that runs in your browser, with three modes: Zombies, a co-op monster survival, plus Free for all and Team deathmatch. Before you play, the page asks you to confirm that you own a physical copy of the original game, which lets it load its hosted game assets, or you can load a ROM from your own copy. On a keyboard, WASD moves, the mouse turns Link and the camera, holding right click aims and left click fires, left click outside of aiming or C swings the sword, Q locks on, Space jumps, R rolls, E is the action button, Shift raises the shield, 1, 2 and 3 pick items and Esc opens the arena menu. Gamepads and touch screens work too, with twin sticks to move and aim. In Zombies you fight rounds of monsters, collect rupees and spend them on new weapons such as the Fairy Bow and on opening up new areas. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a 1998 action-adventure game for the Nintendo 64 from Nintendo, in which Link travels through time to stop Ganondorf and save Hyrule.

title: Total Overdose
author: shydev
description: Note: Currently has some performance and audio issues. This is shydev's work-in-progress browser recompilation of Total Overdose. The game loads automatically when you open the page, showing its progress while it starts, and it runs in a single tab, with the sound playing from whichever tab you used last. It is played with the keyboard, and the project is still being worked on. Total Overdose: A Gunslinger's Tale in Mexico is a 2005 third-person shooter from Deadline Games, published by Eidos Interactive, in which you play Ramiro Cruz and score style points with acrobatic gunplay and special moves across Mexico.

title: Neverball
author: neverball.org
description: This is the official browser version of Neverball from neverball.org, built with Emscripten and gl4es, so nothing needs installing. The arrow keys tilt the floor, moving the mouse tilts it too and left and right click move the camera, the sticks of a gamepad tilt the floor and move the camera, and on a touch screen you swipe to tilt and use another thumb to move the camera. You can start in fullscreen, save replays and watch replays you upload, and custom add-ons (.zip or .pk3 files) load automatically when the game starts. The page offers to refresh when a new version is available, and on a phone it can be added to the home screen to launch like an app. Neverball is a free, open-source puzzle arcade game in which you tilt the floor to roll a ball through an obstacle course before time runs out. A fall or a timeout costs a ball, and collecting coins unlocks the exit and earns extra balls: yellow coins are worth 1, red 5 and blue 10, and every 100 coins gives an extra ball. It was created by Robert Kooima and is developed by the Neverball contributors.

title: Mindustry
author: wasmga.me
description: wasmga.me, a site of games you play in your browser, has Mindustry playable with keyboard and mouse. It offers 35 hand-made maps and more than 250 procedurally generated sectors across the planets Serpulo and Erekir, and a Saves panel that can import a save file and lists scores for whole runs and single levels, for just you or for everyone. You move with WASD (Shift boosts over blocks), pick blocks with 1 to 0, rotate with R, take control of a unit or turret with Ctrl, respawn with V, pause with Space and open the menu with Esc. Left click shoots, places or selects, right click removes or cancels, middle click picks a block, and the scroll wheel zooms or rotates what you are placing. Mindustry is a factory-building, tower defense and real-time strategy game by Anuke and the Mindustry contributors. You build supply chains that feed ammunition to turrets and produce materials, build and command units, capture enemy bases, move liquids, research new blocks and launch resources between sectors. New players should start by researching blocks with the copper and lead the core collects, using mechanical drills on ore to feed the core through conveyors.

title: Pokémon Stadium 2
author: azelf420
file_requirement_review: {"title": "Pokémon Stadium 2", "detail_url": "https://ported2browser.com/ports/01M52FZSRWMVAAB3F6THXNF8MJ", "direct_url": "https://azelf420.github.io/s2w/", "basis": "directory_about_review", "required": true, "optional": false, "disc_image": false, "scope": "required_to_play", "note": "ROM estadounidense propia de Pokemon Stadium 2; el proyecto no incluye datos del juego."}
description: This is a work-in-progress browser port of Pokémon Stadium 2 by azelf420. The game's code is translated ahead of time into WebAssembly from your own ROM, with a runtime standing in for the console's operating system and a WebGPU renderer, so nothing needs installing. No game data is included: you supply your own US ROM, which the page asks for on your first visit and keeps in your browser. It currently boots to the title screen and menus and runs Battle Now! with 3D battles at about 30 fps, the game's native rate, and with sound. On a keyboard, X is A, Z is B, Enter is Start, Shift or Space is Z, Q and E are L and R, I, J, K and L are the C buttons, the arrow keys are the D-pad and WASD is the stick; USB and Bluetooth controllers are detected automatically. Online two-player battles are still in progress, and the Gym Leader Castle, the mini games and the GB Tower have not been tested yet. It needs Chrome or Edge on a desktop computer. Pokémon Stadium 2 is a 2001 Nintendo 64 game from Nintendo in which you battle with Pokémon from the first two generations in 3D arenas, with tournaments, the Gym Leader Castle and a collection of mini games, and it can link to the Game Boy Pokémon games with the Transfer Pak.

title: NFS Underground 2
author: Slayoner
description: Note: Currently has some performance issues. NFS Underground 2 is an experimental browser port of the 2004 PlayStation 2 street racing game by Slayoner, built on the PS2 Web Recomp engine by snuri00 and running on WebAssembly and WebGPU, so nothing needs installing. It offers single player menus and races with audio, graphics and display settings, and an experimental online mode where you create a private room and share its code or search for an opponent, with the players' inputs synced frame by frame. There is also community chat and daily and weekly leaderboards of verified online race wins. Progress is saved to a virtual memory card in your browser, which you can download as a .ps2 file, import or back up. On a keyboard the arrow keys steer, S, D, A and W are the face buttons, Q, E, 1 and 3 are the shoulder buttons and Enter and Backspace are Start and Select, and the keys can be remapped; USB and Bluetooth controllers work, and phones get an on-screen stick and buttons, best in landscape and fullscreen. Race performance is still being optimized and can be slow depending on your hardware, so start at 1x resolution and raise it only if the game stays smooth. The site says it is an independent project, not affiliated with or authorized by the Need for Speed rights holders, and that it is funded by advertising. Need for Speed: Underground 2 is a 2004 street racing game from EA Black Box and Electronic Arts, set in an open city of tuning shops and night races, where you customize your cars and enter circuit, sprint and drift events.

title: Conker's BFD (Multiplayer)
author: conker.wtf
description: conker.wtf is a fan remake of the multiplayer mode of Conker's Bad Fur Day for the browser, built in Rust and WebAssembly. It connects you to online matches, and its status line shows the connection to conker.wtf over WebTransport, so it needs a browser that supports WebTransport. Matches show your rank, a countdown timer, a radar and your current weapon, and the weapons include a rifle and a sniper rifle with a scope. Keyboard and controller are supported, and no Rumble Pak is needed. The project says it is not affiliated with Rare, Microsoft or Nintendo. Conker's Bad Fur Day is a 2001 platform game for the Nintendo 64 from Rare, known for its crude humor. It also has a competitive multiplayer mode, which this project recreates.

title: Hot Shots Golf
author: oldgames.app
description: oldgames.app, a retro game site covering NES, SNES, Game Boy Advance, Game Boy Color, Neo Geo, Sega Genesis, N64 and PS1 titles, has Hot Shots Golf playable in your browser: press Load game on the game's page to start it. Keyboard, controller and touch are all supported. Hot Shots Golf, known as Everybody's Golf in Europe, is a 1997 golf game for the PlayStation from Sony Computer Entertainment, developed by Camelot Software Planning. It is a cartoonish take on golf with colorful graphics, quirky characters, multiple courses and several game modes.

title: Combat Skirmish (CS 1.6)
author: combatskirmish.net
description: Combat Skirmish runs Counter-Strike 1.6, Valve's classic multiplayer shooter, in your browser through WebAssembly on the open-source FWGS engine, with no download, install or account. Quick Join drops you into a live server in seconds, or you can open the Server Browser to pick a map and region, and it uses the same public servers as the Steam version. Modes include Bomb Defusal, Hostage Rescue, Deathmatch, Aim Arena, Gun Game, Zombie Mod, Surf and Bunny Hop on maps such as de_dust2, de_inferno, de_nuke, cs_office and cs_italy, and a Compete option offers ranked 5v5 matches with a party of up to five. The site also offers Sven Co-op, the co-op Half-Life mod. On a keyboard you move with WASD, shoot with the left mouse button and buy weapons with B, gamepads can be used too, phones and tablets get on-screen touch controls, and PC VR works through SteamVR or another OpenXR runtime. The first load caches the engine and maps stream in as you need them. The site says it is not affiliated with Valve. Counter-Strike began as a Half-Life mod and became a Valve game in 2000: terrorists and counter-terrorists play short rounds, buying weapons with the money they earn and either planting and defusing a bomb or rescuing hostages. Sven Co-op is a free Half-Life mod in which players work through story maps together.

title: Tekken: Dark Resurrection
author: gacid
file_requirement_review: {"title": "Tekken: Dark Resurrection", "detail_url": "https://ported2browser.com/ports/01M4ZTRTVENYXSAPMVX1HHCNXG", "direct_url": "https://tkdr-recomp.pages.dev/", "basis": "directory_about_review", "required": true, "optional": false, "disc_image": true, "scope": "required_to_play", "note": "Volcado propio ISO/CSO de Tekken DR y EBOOT descifrado; el runtime declara lectura local."}
runtime_observation: {"url": "https://tkdr-recomp.pages.dev/", "state": "hosted_download_started", "note": "La ficha declara ISO/CSO y EBOOT propios. El destino actual ofrece descargar aproximadamente 1 GB desde su servidor; al pulsar Play se observó contacting the game server/Running, sin seleccionar archivos. Requisito de la ficha en conflicto con el lanzador actual; partida sin comprobar.", "rendered_game_scene": false, "requirements_conflict": true, "observed_on": "2026-11-15", "method": "existing_chrome_windows_ui", "physical_controller_tested": false}
description: Note: Currently has some performance issues. This is a browser recompilation of Tekken: Dark Resurrection (the USA PSP disc, ULUS-10139) by gacid. The game's executable is translated ahead of time into WebAssembly, with a runtime that reimplements the PSP's system libraries, so no CPU emulation is involved, and the graphics are drawn through WebGL 2. The project does not include the game: you need your own disc dump (an ISO or CSO) and a decrypted EBOOT, which can be dumped with PPSSPP, and you drop or pick them on the page. The page says the files are read on your computer and never uploaded, and the disc is stored compressed in your browser so later visits only need Play. It needs a recent browser with WebGL 2, and phones and tablets get full-screen touch controls. On a keyboard, the arrows are the D-pad, Enter and Space are Start and Select, Z, X, C and S are the face buttons and Q and W are L and R; gamepads, arcade sticks and hitboxes are detected automatically, and F1 opens settings for rebinding, SOCD modes, internal resolution, the renderer and HD texture packs. The project reports 60 fps at up to 4x resolution, with save data and movies with sound, tested from boot to Quick Battle with other modes less explored, and without SAS reverb or ad-hoc multiplayer. It describes itself as an unofficial fan project that is not affiliated with Bandai Namco or Sony. Tekken: Dark Resurrection is a 2006 fighting game for the PlayStation Portable from Namco and Eighting, a handheld version of the arcade update of Tekken 5.

title: Guitar Hero 3
author: Chris
file_requirement_review: {"title": "Guitar Hero 3", "detail_url": "https://ported2browser.com/ports/01M4ZTRTTVV7VXERJHAZTYTGNG", "direct_url": "https://gh3.thediaryofchris.net/index.html", "basis": "directory_about_review", "required": true, "optional": false, "disc_image": false, "scope": "required_to_play", "note": "Carpeta de Guitar Hero 3 con GH3.exe y DATA, o archivos individuales. La prueba de sonido sin juego no equivale a jugar."}
description: Note: Supports guitar controllers. Guitar Hero Browser Edition is an unofficial fan project from Chris that plays songs from your own copy of Guitar Hero III for PC on a note highway in your browser. It includes no songs or artwork: you choose the folder that contains GH3.exe or its DATA folder, or pick individual files, and the page reads them on your computer without uploading them. If the game is on another computer, you can run a local server there and enter a connection code, and a built-in soundcheck riff plays even without the game. On a keyboard, you hold a fret key and press strum, and the keys can be rebound. Guitar controllers are supported: Santroller in HID mode, CRKD in PC or KeyJam mode, and XInput guitars such as the Xbox 360 one, with direct connection needing Chrome or Edge. You can practise chosen sections, slow a song to 90%, 75% or half speed, watch autoplay, change the difficulty and part, correct audio delay and input lag, and use no-fail mode and lefty flip. Display options include hyperspeed, hit flames, a custom background, highway designs, the band and crowd, and an FPS counter. Scores are stored in your browser under a name you choose and can be exported and imported to compare with friends; there is no online multiplayer. Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock is a 2007 rhythm game from Neversoft, published by Activision, in which you play along to rock songs on a guitar-shaped controller through a career of gigs and boss battles. This port plays songs from its PC version.

title: FIFA Street 2
author: Slayoner
description: This is a browser version of FIFA Street 2 by Slayoner. The page describes itself as an independent project inspired by the PES 6 web port by OptiProjects, and it credits snuri00's PS2 Web Recomp as its web engine, with a WebGPU graphics option. It loads the game automatically, with no installation and no disc image or files from you: click Jugar (Play), wait for "Preparando el juego…" to finish, then click inside the game image. The interface is in Spanish by default, with English, Portuguese, French, German and Italian available. Controls are the arrow keys to move, I, J, K and L as the right stick and S, D, A and W for passing, shooting, crossing and through balls, with remappable keys, plus any standard USB or Bluetooth controller; on phones it shows on-screen sticks and buttons and suggests landscape and fullscreen. Settings cover volume, an internal resolution of 1x to 3x (the page recommends starting at 1x), image smoothing and a memory card you can download or import in the PCSX2 format. Online play is experimental, with two players per room, private room codes, a nickname, chat and daily and weekly win rankings, and the page recommends Chrome or Edge. The page shows ads. FIFA Street 2 is a 2006 arcade-style street football game from EA Canada, published by EA Sports BIG, with small-sided matches on street pitches built around tricks and combos. It was released for PlayStation 2, Xbox and GameCube.

title: NBA Street V3
author: recomp-code
description: Note: After the initial load, the game may require a refresh. This is a browser version of NBA Street V3 by recomp-code, built from a recompilation of the PlayStation 2 game: the game's code is recompiled to WebAssembly and drawn with a WebGL2 renderer based on Play!. The project describes its browser version as experimental, and the page that hosts it has a Spanish interface, with a Jugar (Play) button that appears once the game has downloaded for the first time. The page does not ask you for a disc image or any files. Its settings let you choose a resolution from native up to 4x, turn HD textures on or off, adjust sound buffering for phones or fast PCs, and enable online play. Controls are the arrows or WASD to move, Z, X, C and V plus Q, E, 1 and 3 for the action buttons and Enter for Start, and controllers are supported too. NBA Street V3 is a 2005 arcade-style streetball game from EA Canada, published by EA Sports BIG, with trick combos and Gamebreaker dunks played on city courts such as Venice Beach and Rucker Park. It was released for PlayStation 2, Xbox and GameCube.

title: Diablo 2 Survivors
author: Framara
description: Note: This is an unofficial fan project that is not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard Entertainment. D2 Survivors is a fan-made, survivors-style browser game set in the world of Diablo II. You fight waves of monsters in Act I locations such as the Blood Moor while a timer and a kill count run, and every level-up offers a choice of three new or upgraded skills, with options to reroll, skip or banish a choice. You also collect gold and gear: open your inventory to equip items, and visit Charsi to shop or gamble. On a keyboard, Enter starts or continues, Esc pauses, I opens the inventory, T visits Charsi and G gambles, and the mouse picks up, equips and sells items; touch is supported too. The pause menu has Save and exit game as well as sound and music options. Diablo II is Blizzard North's 2000 action role-playing game, in which a lone hero fights through hordes of demons and undead, collecting loot and building a character from one of several classes.

title: Mega Man Legends (Series)
author: oldgames.app
description: oldgames.app, a retro game site covering NES, SNES, Game Boy Advance, Game Boy Color, Neo Geo, Sega Genesis, N64 and PS1 titles, has the three PlayStation Mega Man Legends games playable in your browser: press Load game on a game's page to start it. Keyboard, controller and touch are all supported. Mega Man Legends is Capcom's 3D action-adventure series starring Mega Man Volnutt, who explores dungeons, battles enemies and uncovers ancient mysteries in a world that mixes exploration, combat and light RPG elements. It spans Mega Man Legends (1997), Mega Man Legends 2 (2000) and the spin-off The Misadventures of Tron Bonne (1999), in which Tron Bonne leads her Servbots on missions to gather resources and save her family.

title: No One Lives Forever
author: Brightwork Digital
description: Note: This is an unofficial, fan-made project that is not affiliated with Monolith Productions or any rights holder, and the PlayStation 2-only chapters have rough edges. This is a fan-made browser version of No One Lives Forever by Brightwork Digital, with nothing to install. The game's engine was never released, so the port runs on a new engine that the site says was written with AI agents and checked against the original game. It includes all 16 missions across 65 levels, the Game of the Year bonus mission and the chapters made for the PlayStation 2 version, which have never been on PC before. There is a jukebox for the game's score, and optional accounts keep your saved games across computers. Keyboard and mouse play uses the game's default keys with WASD to move, Xbox and PlayStation controllers are supported, and touch uses on-screen sticks and buttons, best with the phone held sideways. No One Lives Forever is a 2000 first-person spy action game from Monolith Productions, published by Fox Interactive. You play Cate Archer, a former cat burglar turned agent in a comic 1960s spy world, with missions that mix stealth, gunfights and gadgets. A Game of the Year Edition followed in 2001 with an extra mission.

title: Happy Wheels
author: Totaljerkface.com
description: Note: Happy Wheels contains graphic cartoon violence. This is the web version of Happy Wheels, reached from the news page on totaljerkface.com, the site of Fancy Force, LLC. The page says the full version is playable only there and credits kwlsh for the porting work. It announces the game's Steam release, warns that servers may be strained by launch traffic with Discord as the place to report problems, and lists controller and Steam Deck improvements, offline support, achievements and bug fixes as planned updates. Happy Wheels is a physics-based game from 2010 by Fancy Force in which you try to reach the finish line on user-created tracks, with your limbs still being attached optional. You choose from a cast of characters and vehicles, and the game includes a level editor for making and sharing your own levels.

title: Tremulous
author: Justin Luong and Auriga
description: This is the Web Edition of Tremulous, ported to the web by Justin Luong and Auriga, with WebNova360 running the servers, the AI players and the fixes. It has two servers: Overmind Arena for 20 against 20 and Reactor Skirmish for 10 against 10, where AI players fill empty seats and step aside as people join. The servers are web-only, so players of the desktop game can't join them. The first load downloads about 250 MB of game data, which is cached afterwards. On a desktop you play with the keyboard and mouse, and on phones and tablets there are on-screen thumb controls, with landscape mode recommended and adding the page to the home screen giving full screen on iPhone. It is free, with no ads or account, and the game data is CC BY-SA 2.5 while the code is GPL. Tremulous is a free, open-source game from Dark Legion Development, released in 2006, that blends a team-based FPS with elements of an RTS. Players choose between two races, aliens and humans, and build working structures in the game, the most important of which spawn players, so the designated builders have to keep spawn structures up. Other structures give automated base defense, healing and more. Aliens evolve from dretches toward tyrants and build around the Overmind, while humans buy weapons and gear and build bases around the Reactor.

title: Ballance
author: Fayazara Ahmed
description: This browser version of Ballance is by Fayazara Ahmed and has been ported to WebGL so that it runs in the browser. Its menu offers Start, Highscore, Options (Graphics, Controls, Sound and a Download offline option), Credits and Exit, a controller connects automatically when you press any of its buttons, and the credits screen reproduces the original Cyparade team credits from Berlin, 2004. The level selection menu offers all 12 original levels. Ballance is a 2004 puzzle game from the German studio Cyparade, published by Atari, in which you steer a sphere to the end of each of the game's 12 linear levels. The surreal environments have you transform between three different materials to push boxes, spheres and other objects out of the way and clear a path.

title: Manic Miner
author: Jindřich Šaršon
description: This browser version is a JavaScript port of Manic Miner by Jindřich Šaršon, with a classic and a remastered version, developed to give the same gameplay experience as the original, timing included. You can choose Original or Remastered and Beeper 48K or AY 128K sound, switch the sound off, go fullscreen and press the Start cavern button to begin. On the keyboard, the Q to T and Y to P rows or the left and right arrow keys move Willy, Space on the bottom row or the up arrow jumps, Enter starts, Esc quits, the A to G row pauses and the H to L row turns the tune on and off, as on the original Spectrum. On a phone, turn it sideways to play. Manic Miner is a platform game written for the ZX Spectrum by Matthew Smith and released by Bug-Byte in 1983, and later re-released by Software Projects. It is the first game in the Miner Willy series and one of the earliest platform games, inspired by the Atari 800 game Miner 2049er, and it has since been ported to many home computers and consoles.

title: Compositor
author: Scott Zackrison
description: This is the browser version of Compositor. It opens projects from the Mac app, as a project folder or a zipped project, or lets you start a new canvas, open an image or drop one onto the page, or open a sample project. Its menus are File, Edit, Select, Image, Filter, Layer, View and Help, there is a Layers panel, and the Move / Transform tool's hint says that Shift frees the ratio, Alt scales from the center, Ctrl-drag on a handle distorts, Alt-drag duplicates and Ctrl-click picks a layer. Compositor is a free, open-source, lightweight image editor and Photoshop alternative by Robbie Tilton, built for compositing and post-processing. It has layers and folders, layer and clipping masks, blend modes, selection tools, adjustment layers, filters such as Gaussian blur, motion blur and lens correction, grain and noise, liquify and smear, spot healing, a clone stamp, a brush and built-in background removal. Its desktop version is a native Mac app released under the MIT license, and it is not affiliated with or endorsed by Adobe.

title: Dragon Ball Z: BT 3
author: Slayoner
description: This browser version is Budokai T3 Web Online, an independent, non-profit project that runs Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3 on PC with no installation, using what its page credits as a Tenkaichi3Decomp engine and a WebGL 2 renderer with 1x to 3x resolution scaling. It offers online two-player duels through a private room code or matchmaking, which is labeled experimental: matchmaking can be slow or find no opponent, and the match stops if the connection or sync drops. Each online player runs the game on their own PC, and both must finish loading before the match starts. Saves are stored locally with backup and import options, and the settings cover volume, resolution, texture filtering and a 30 or 60 fps option. The default keyboard layout is the arrow keys for the D-pad, W, A, S and D for the left stick, K and L for the cross and circle buttons, J and I for square and triangle, U and O for L1 and R1, 7 and 9 for L2 and R2, Enter for Start and Right Shift for Select. Press F1 in the game to change the controls, or use a USB or Bluetooth controller. The site recommends Chrome or Edge at 1x resolution with the tab kept visible. Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3 is a 2007 one-on-one fighting game from Spike, published by Namco Bandai Games and Atari and based on Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball. It has over 162 characters with their own moves and combos, and you fight a friend or the computer in many game modes, across stages with different weather and time conditions.

title: AssaultCube
author: CriShoux
description: This is a browser version of AssaultCube by CriShoux, built from the game's own C++ source compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten and drawn with WebGL, so it runs offline in the tab after downloading about 43 MB of game data. It has all 44 official maps, the weapons, the sound and the bot AI, with Bot Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, OSOK (one shot, one kill), Pistol Frenzy and Survival modes and a choice of how many bots you play against. Online multiplayer is not available in the browser and needs the desktop game. Move with W, A, S and D, aim with the mouse and click to fire, right-click to scope or use the alternate fire, press Space to jump, Shift to crouch, R to reload, 1 to 4 for the weapon slots, G for a quick grenade, Tab for the scores and Esc for the menu, which also frees the mouse. Your settings and nickname are saved in the browser. AssaultCube is a free, open-source first-person shooter based on the Cube engine, developed by Rabid Viper Productions and released in 2008. It takes place in realistic environments with fast, arcade-style gameplay.

title: Pokémon Redstone
author: MozeTech
description: Pokémon Redstone is a free, unofficial fan project by MozeTech that mixes Pokémon with Minecraft. You play as Steve in a Pokémon-style overworld with a minimap, hearts, hunger and a Minecraft hotbar, mining, placing blocks and eating as you go, and you can be slain by mobs such as zombies. Meeting a wild Pokémon, such as a Rattata, starts a Pokémon-style battle where Steve fights with moves like Punch. The title screen also offers a Join co-op option. Move with the arrow keys or WASD, hold Z to mine, attack or talk, press X to use, place or eat, Space to jump, Shift to sprint, E for the inventory, Q to drop, 1 to 9, the mouse wheel or C and V for the hotbar, Enter for the menu, J for the map and M to toggle music; phones get on-screen touch buttons. It combines two series: Pokémon, from Nintendo, Game Freak and Creatures, and Minecraft, from Mojang and Microsoft. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo, Game Freak, Creatures, The Pokémon Company, Mojang or Microsoft, and Pokémon and Minecraft are trademarks of their respective owners.

title: Clover Pit
author: breadbb
description: This browser version of CloverPit is by breadbb and is hosted on GN-Math's games site. It runs in the browser without a separate installation and plays with a keyboard and mouse. CloverPit is a 2025 slot machine game from Panik Arcade, published by Future Friends Games. You wake up in a rusty, narrow cell, standing over a dangerously unstable grate. Someone has kidnapped you and demands payment, and your only way out is to play the slot machine and pay off your debt, without falling, literally, into ruin.

title: DOOM Multiplayer
author: Cloudflare
description: This is Cloudflare's multiplayer DOOM demo, also known as Edge Doom and Silent Space Marine: the original game running as Chocolate Doom compiled to WebAssembly, with its network code replaced so that game traffic travels over WebSockets through Cloudflare Workers. It loads the original game's shareware doom1.wad. Up to four players can play deathmatch or co-op, or you can play solo, and the host's game acts as the server, with a shareable link to invite others. You aim with the mouse and press F for fullscreen. DOOM's original lockstep networking means every player waits on the slowest connection, and a player who closes their browser abruptly can disrupt the game. DOOM is a 1993 first-person shooter from id Software. Hours after distress messages arrive from Phobos and Deimos vanishes completely, you and your team are sent to investigate the Union Aerospace Corporation's facilities on Mars. Left alone with only a pistol, you fight your way through a complex of demons.

title: Call of Mini: Dino Hunter
author: framkallare
description: This browser version of Call of Mini: Dino Hunter is by framkallare. It plays with a keyboard on desktop or with touch controls on a phone, which has to be held in landscape, and it has a fullscreen option. Call of Mini: Dino Hunter is a 2013 mobile shooter from Triniti Interactive Studios. Dinosaurs emerge from the ancient forest after hiding for decades, and as the descendant of a great hunter family you hone your skills to live up to your father's expectations. You fight your way through hordes of giant lizards and collect items to craft and upgrade various weapons.

title: Holiday Island
author: PlayClassic.games
description: Note: the German version of this site links to a German-language copy of the game on ClassicReload. Holiday Island is a 1996 business simulation game for Windows developed by the German company Sunflowers. You juggle funds to build hotels, accommodation, leisure activities and restaurants on an island resort. The number and location of these matters, as does the interconnectivity between different facilities.

title: PokéSurvivor
author: JPTER78
description: PokéSurvivor is a free, non-profit fan-made survival game starring Pokémon, inspired by Survivor.io. You pick a companion from the starters of every region, enter a dungeon and fight waves of enemies. Between runs you spend coins on upgrades for each Pokémon, which only apply when you play with that one, and there is also a gacha for Pokémon and shinies, missions, achievements, a Pokédex and a leaderboard for how long you survive. You can play as a guest, whose progress is not saved, or sign in to keep it, and group runs support up to four players connected directly between browsers. Move with WASD or by dragging a finger, pick level-up rewards with 1 to 3 and reroll with R, and pause with Esc; phones must be held in landscape. The game is free, with no ads or purchases, and optional donations only cover server and domain costs and give no in-game advantage. Its sprites come from SpriteCollab (CC BY-NC 4.0), its Pokédex data from PokeAPI, its font is Pixelify Sans, and its music and sound effects are original. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo, Creatures Inc., GAME FREAK or The Pokémon Company, and it has no official cryptocurrency, token or NFT.

title: Terraria
author: Mercury Workshop
description: Note: creating a new world takes a long time to load, so expect a wait the first time you start one. This browser version of Terraria is listed on gn-math, a site that launches browser games, and works with a keyboard or a controller. Terraria is a 2D sandbox action-adventure game from Re-Logic, released in 2011, with platforming and role-playing elements. You create a character and are placed in a procedurally generated world, where you dig, build, craft gear and fight enemies and bosses, alone or with friends.

title: Superfighters
author: decxx1
description: This browser version of Superfighters is an HTML5 build by decxx1, which adds 60 fps gameplay, local play for up to four players and online multiplayer. The menu offers Play, Multiplayer and Settings in English and Spanish, with Versus, Stages, Survival, Practice and Tutorial modes, zero to seven bot opponents and weapons from pistols and shotguns to a bazooka and a flamethrower. Players three and four have no default keyboard keys, so controllers are recommended for local multiplayer. Superfighters Deluxe is a 2D multiplayer action game from Mythologic Interactive in which little flat-headed men fight to the death in small, highly destructible arenas. Johan Hjärpe designed it and made the art, Alexander Siigur programmed it, and HZLancer composed the music.

title: OVZ (Modern Warfare 2)
author: OVZ Alpha
description: This is the OVZ Alpha, a work-in-progress browser version of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 multiplayer. Its own menu calls it OVZ: Global Flashpoint, and its message of the day warns that there will be bugs. It first downloads about 11 MB of game files, and matchmaking and match start unlock when that finishes. You pick a name, then play public matches through matchmaking, start a private match or invite a friend, and the menu shows how many players are online. Matches run on a ten-minute timer with grenade and flashbang slots and a killstreak counter, and the game asks you to click to lock the mouse cursor inside the game. Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 is a 2009 first-person shooter from Infinity Ward, published by Activision. Its multiplayer has you earn killstreak rewards and customize your loadout with perks across a wide range of maps and modes.

title: Super Mario Zombies
author: 0xRishi
description: Super Mario Zombies is a fan-made, non-commercial mash-up by 0xRishi that plays like the Zombies mode of Call of Duty: Black Ops, with Nintendo's Mario characters as the undead: Mario, Luigi, Yoshi, Bowser, Boo, Dry Bones and more come at you. It opens on a press-any-key title screen, has a settings menu and a full screen button, and offers a map selection screen. Call of Duty: Black Ops is a 2010 first-person shooter by Treyarch, published by Activision. Its Zombies mode has you survive wave after wave of the undead, earning points to buy weapons and open up new areas of the map.

title: Skate 3
author: aaddpp
file_requirement_review: {"title": "Skate 3", "detail_url": "https://ported2browser.com/ports/01M4RSDRCPXRTKPRT50EBRRCW5", "direct_url": "https://skate.aaddpp.lol/", "basis": "directory_about_review", "required": true, "optional": false, "disc_image": false, "scope": "required_to_play", "note": "Datos de una copia propia convertida de Skate 3."}
description: This browser version is an unofficial fan game by aaddpp, a Rust engine for Skate 3 that its page says is not made, endorsed or supported by EA or Black Box. No game content is hosted on the site: you need your own legally owned copy of Skate 3, converted on your own machine, and the game data streams from that converted copy. The first load is the slow one, settings are saved in the browser, and the page asks you not to close the tab while the game is loading. Skate 3 is a 2010 skateboarding game from EA Black Box. It adds a co-op mode where teammates complete challenges together, a beefed-up Hall of Meat mode that rewards epic bails, the skate.School training and the skate.Create tools for user-created content.

title: R.E.P.O.
author: Genizy
description: This browser version is a Unity WebGL build by Genizy, hosted on truffled. It opens in an embedded player that shows a loading screen while the game data downloads, so keep the page open until the game appears. R.E.P.O. (Retrieve, Extract and Profit Operation) is a survival horror game from the Swedish studio Semiwork, made in Unity and released in 2025 as an online cooperative game for up to six players on PC. You locate valuable physics-based objects in procedurally generated environments and carry them carefully to extraction points without damaging them, all while avoiding hostile creatures. Between levels you spend your earnings on permanent upgrades, weapons and tools at a service station, and teammates are meant to coordinate by voice.

title: Oni
author: spade-skill
description: This browser port by spade-skill runs Oni's original engine, compiled to WebAssembly, with the original game data. You choose what to load first: the main menu plus the warehouse and tutorial, which covers the menu and the first mission, or the entire campaign (about 554 MiB, plus engine memory). Intro and outro movies play from converted copies, and you can import and download saves; download yours before closing if the browser's storage is unavailable. The original controls are WASD to move, F to punch, C to kick, Space to jump, Shift to crouch, Ctrl for action, Q to swap, E to drop, R to reload and Tab for the hypo. Click the canvas to focus it and capture the mouse, and press Escape to release the mouse. Oni is a 2001 action game from Bungie in which Konoko, an elite agent of a tech crimes task force, fights the Syndicate while haunted by the demons of her past, mixing hand-to-hand combat and gunplay.

title: Grand Theft Auto V
author: deloskiyt.pl
description: This browser version is by deloskiyt.pl. It downloads the game data when it opens, with a loading counter in megabytes, then asks you to choose Story Mode (Enter) or Sandbox Mode (Space). You can play GTA V's story, or play the sandbox on the Grand Theft Auto V map or on the Grand Theft Auto VI map. Grand Theft Auto V is a vast open world game from Rockstar North, released in 2013 and set in Los Santos, a sprawling sun-soaked metropolis struggling to stay afloat in an era of economic uncertainty and cheap reality TV. It blends storytelling and gameplay in new ways as you repeatedly jump in and out of the lives of its three protagonists.

title: Friday Night Funkin'
author: Gamaverse
description: Gamaverse hosts Friday Night Funkin' in the browser: the original version, with the Pitstop 2 Update included, alongside many fan-made mods with new looks and songs. The site describes them all as Chromebook-optimized and unblocked, and suggests playing the original first for some practice, since the mods can be quite challenging. Five popular mods are featured below: Clay Mod, Smoke 'Em Out Struggle, V.S. Whitty Full Week, VS Impostor and Doki Doki Takeover Plus!. Friday Night Funkin' is a music rhythm game made by ninjamuffin99 and the Funkin' Crew, known for easy-to-learn but hard-to-master button-mashing gameplay, catchy songs and memorable characters.

title: You Don't Know Jack
author: ydkjs_eu
description: This browser version is a fan work by ydkjs_eu, part of the You Don't Know JavaScript project. The author extracted the original art and sound and rewrote the engine in JavaScript, and says it has no connection with Jackbox Games and is free, ad-free and non-profit. It comes as a UK edition, with French and German editions linked for those site languages. You can start a quick seven-question local game for one, two or three players, start a new multiplayer game, or join one by code or through a public session. The page calls it a sample of the full game with a lot still missing, though the full version can now be played online. It works best in Firefox and Chrome and can be played full screen; smartphone browsers do not handle it well. You Don't Know Jack is the 1995 original of Jellyvision's comedic trivia series, later continued by Jackbox Games, released for Windows and Mac.

title: Spore Origins
author: nomadic_ua
description: This browser version is a remake by nomadic_ua, made with Defold and listed on itch.io as a simulation game. Spore Origins is the 2008 mobile spin-off of Spore, built around a single phase of the larger game: the cell phase. You try to survive as a multicellular organism in a tide pool, and you can upgrade your creature as in the main game. Electronic Arts published it.

title: Amazing Alex
author: nomadic_ua
description: This browser version is a remake by nomadic_ua, made as a 2D HTML5 game. Its itch.io page states that no generative AI was used. Amazing Alex is a physics-based puzzle game by Rovio Entertainment, released for phones in 2012. It centres on Rube Goldberg machines and is based on Casey's Contraptions, whose rights Rovio bought.

title: Master of Defence
author: nomadic_ua
description: This browser version is a remake by nomadic_ua, described on itch.io as a classic tower defence game remake. It was made with Godot and runs as an HTML5 game. Master of Defense is a 3D tower defense strategy game released for Windows in 2006 and published by Big Fish Games.

title: Minecraft Web Client
author: Sandexzx
description: Minecraft Web Client is a Minecraft client clone that runs in your browser. It is the Prismarine Web Client V2 presented by Sandexzx, at version 2.3.0 when this entry was written, and its start screen asks you to mind the bugs and have fun. You can connect to Java servers, or play singleplayer: create worlds and play offline, explore maps from a provider, or load any Java world save. There is also an options menu. It can be played with a keyboard, a controller or touch controls. Minecraft is (c) Mojang Studios / Microsoft, and this is an unofficial browser client.

title: Superflight
author: zay
description: Superflight is a fast, easy-to-learn wingsuit flying game with an endless supply of beautiful procedurally generated maps. It is a good way to unwind for half an hour while chasing your latest high score. GrizzlyGames made Superflight and released it for Windows in November 2017. This browser version is by zay and is hosted on wasm.rip. It can be played with a keyboard or a controller.

title: wosu!
author: Mostlime12195
description: wosu! is an unofficial, open-source osu!standard client that runs entirely in your browser, with nothing to install. Mostlime12195 made it as the successor to WebOsu 2, itself a continuation of the original WebOsu. osu! is a rhythm game in which you click circles on the screen to the rhythm of the music. Beatmaps come from community mirrors, or you can import your own .osz files, and several beatmaps are included. Scoring and judgement follow the rules of osu! closely but can still differ from the official game, and only the osu!standard mode is supported. It has mods (Easy, No Fail, Half Time, Daycore, Hard Rock, Sudden Death, Perfect, Double Time, Nightcore, Hidden, Flashlight, Relax, Autopilot and Spun Out) and an Autoplay mode, a full HUD with difficulty bars and click counters, storyboards, beatmap skins and hitsounds, background video, background dim and blur, a now-playing panel and notifications. Your settings are saved in your browser, and a WebGPU renderer can be turned on in the settings. You hit with Z and X, the mouse buttons or by tapping, and the keys can be rebound in the settings. Esc pauses and Space skips the intro. The older WebOsu 2 is still online for devices that struggle with wosu!. wosu! is not affiliated with or endorsed by ppy, and osu! is a trademark of ppy Pty Ltd.

title: Nazi Zombies: Portable
author: NZ:P Team
description: Nazi Zombies: Portable, or NZ:P, is a free, open-source recreation of Call of Duty: Zombies built by the NZ:P Team on modified forks of the 1996 Quake engine. It has been in development since 2009 and is an unofficial fan project. The engine is licensed under the GNU General Public License version 2, and the project's assets under CC-BY-SA 4.0. The game aims to match the zombies mode of Call of Duty: World at War on a general level, with minor differences, and adds a few small gameplay-smoothing touches from Call of Duty: Black Ops. You hold out against waves of zombies using barricades, wall weapons, the mystery box, Perk-A-Cola machines and power-ups. You can play solo or with up to four players online. Most World at War maps and their unique features are not represented yet. The browser version runs on WebGL. NZ:P also has builds for Windows, Linux, the PlayStation Portable and Vita, the Nintendo 3DS and Switch, and the TI-Nspire CX II. No stable releases are marked: builds are published as nightly releases. Players can make their own maps. The project's documentation covers TrenchBroom setup, mapping features, JSON data-driving and running a dedicated server with map rotation and voting. Credits: the NZ:P Team made the game, and community mapmakers have contributed maps.

title: Moon Child FE
author: Mors
description: Moon Child FE, where FE stands for Friend Edition, is a free, modern source port of Moon Child, the 1997 Windows 95 platformer by Team Hoi, published by Valkieser Publishing. It is the work of Mors and is based on the later iOS release, with features such as the menu layout and the full-motion videos restored from the original Windows 95 version. The game drew renewed attention in 2026, after which its source code was released and fan ports appeared. In the game, a green elf called Moon Child is sent by the moon to protect the planet Utopia from a techno-virus, carried by a meteor, that is turning it into a lifeless machine world. You run and jump through four worlds, with a jetpack arriving in the third, and you must collect at least 77 of the 84 Dark Diamonds to reach the final psychedelic level. The port adds a browser version with automatic saving and loading, remappable keyboard controls and controller support with a fixed mapping. Pressing Start on a gamepad mid-level returns you to the map, since there is no pause menu, as in the original. It also offers fullscreen and windowed modes, 50 and 60 FPS with Vsync, shimmer-free scaling, a Speedrun Mode with a timer, an Easier Shooting option for the jetpack controls, a Safe Visuals option for the final level, higher-quality audio, alternate title music and updated credits. A few players have reported bugs, such as browser progress being lost. The page states that no generative AI was used. Credits: the source port is by Mors, the original code by Reinier van Vliet, the original graphics by Metin Seven, and the original music and sounds by Ramon Braumuller.

title: Messenger
author: Abeto
description: Messenger is a free browser game built with WebGL. Vicente Lucendo and Michael Sungaila developed it, Abeto, a studio that makes interactive realtime experiences, published it on 25 September 2025, and Kevin Colombin composed its lo-fi music. You play a young mail carrier who delivers parcels and letters around a very small alien planet. The deliveries are often humorous, and the places you visit include a power plant, a forest and a city. The planet is tiny enough to cross in minutes but feels alive, and because it is a sphere, walking around it can feel disorienting at first. Other players are visible in the world, and you can talk to them with emoji, follow them or just hang out. You can also customize your character's outfit, from clothes to hair. The game can be played on a phone too, according to Wikipedia and press coverage. Critics praised its detail, its art style and its relaxing take on fetch quests, and some found it remarkable that a game this polished runs in a browser.

title: Cave Story
author: midzer.de
description: Cave Story is the freeware 2D platform adventure that Daisuke "Pixel" Amaya of Studio Pixel released for Windows on 20 December 2004. You play Quote, an amnesiac robot who explores a cave on a floating island, collecting experience crystals to power up his weapons, and the game is widely seen as one of the most influential indie games and a spark of the Metroidvania revival. This port by midzer runs it in the browser on NXEngine-evo, a refactored fork of the open-source NXEngine rewrite. NXEngine-evo moves the engine to SDL2 and adds widescreen support up to Full HD, animated character portraits, localization support and custom soundtrack support. The page asks you to click to load the game, and it downloads about 9 MB first.

title: Call of Duty Webports
author: Luckey Faraday
description: Note: controller support may vary between ports. Call of Duty: The Web Collection is a repository of Call of Duty maps that you can play in your browser. Its page, presented by Luckey Faraday, describes it as an unofficial fan-made collection that is not affiliated with Activision or Treyarch, and it asks you to choose a map and play. The five maps currently listed are Kino der Toten, a Black Ops Zombies map that can be played solo or in two to four player co-op; Moon, another Black Ops Zombies map; Hijacked, a Black Ops II shooter map; Nuketown 2025, also a Black Ops II shooter map; and Cheese Cube, a Black Ops III custom Zombies map. Each map is its own web port, so controls and controller support can differ from one to the next. The page says the collection spans three generations of the series. It accepts donations toward its hosting costs, and Call of Duty and the original game assets belong to their respective owners.

title: Advance Wars By Web
author: Aaron Marriner
description: Advance Wars By Web, or AWBW, is a free fan-made site that lets you play Advance Wars against other people in your browser, with nothing to download. Aaron Marriner created it in 2004 as an email-chess-style version of Advance Wars, before Advance Wars: Dual Strike was released. It is mainly based on Advance Wars 2: Black Hole Rising, with elements from the first game and Dual Strike. The official Game Boy Advance games had no online play, so AWBW offers close-enough multiplayer for the series. Games are turn-based and can be played one on one, in teams or as free-for-alls of up to 16 players. All 28 Commanding Officers from Advance Wars 1, 2 and Dual Strike are playable, there are custom armies, and you can search thousands of user-made maps, browse them by category or design your own. Live games match players in real time through a live queue and a live league, and the Global League is a ranked ladder. Tournaments run regularly, and a vacation mode freezes your games while you are away. A move planner and a damage calculator help you plan your turns, and the site has an FAQ and tutorials. It works on computers and on mobile devices, and it has no audio. After the original developer stepped back, community developers took over, and a 2021 interface update added real-time games, map animations, the calculator and the planner. Registration is free with a username and password, and donations are accepted through Patreon. Advance Wars is copyrighted by Nintendo and Intelligent Systems, and the site says all images belong to their respective owners. This is an unofficial fan project.

title: Tweetcraft
author: jaivin
description: Note: to create your own world, you have to make a post on X.com. Joining pre-existing worlds has no such requirement. The game contains paid VIP and sponsorship benefits. Tweetcraft is a fan-made, Minecraft-style sandbox game by jaivin that runs in the browser and can be played from inside X, formerly Twitter, hence the cover's "Playable in the timeline!". It was posted on 6 October 2026 and drew more than 5 million views, according to press reports. The developer says no Minecraft assets were used, and it has no connection to Mojang or Microsoft. Worlds are shared servers. The multiplayer list lets you search for worlds or hosts, sort by most players and filter what is shown. Each world lists its host's X handle, its player count out of 1,000 and how many blocks have been built, and you can join one or create a new world. Chat and an inventory are built in, and a Save your progress button keeps your progress. On a computer, press reports say WASD moves, Space jumps, the left mouse button attacks and holding the right mouse button turns the camera. On a phone, on-screen buttons cover the menu, inventory, chat, hit, use and drop. The game is free to join, but it has paid VIP and sponsorship benefits: the world list and the corner of the screen in game carry sponsored entries, and worlds can be sponsored.

title: Binding of Isaac: Repentance
author: Utka
description: This is a browser port of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance by Utka. The page calls the game The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+. The author says they ported it to the web almost in its entirety with Claude Opus 5.5, and that all items, synergies, bosses and saves are intact. It also supports online co-op. Saves are kept in your browser's storage, and a save panel on the page lets you export them as a .zip or .json file, import them again, or reset them. The first load shows a progress bar while the game starts up. The original game is Edmund McMillen's roguelike The Binding of Isaac, and Repentance, released in 2021 with Nicalis, is its largest expansion.

title: Mario 64
author: Oliver Sauter
description: This is a browser version of Super Mario 64 by Oliver Sauter, who posts as @olivers_tools. It is built on the sm64ex PC port, which comes from the game's decompilation, and on the sm64coopdx co-op mod, and it was made with the help of AI. Sauter announced it on 7 October 2026, and every level is playable. On startup you choose single-player or multiplayer. Multiplayer supports up to 12 players running through the same world: join quickly or create a private room, enter a nickname, pick a character and a map, and play either the classic way, collecting stars to unlock stages, or with everything unlocked from the start. A random option drops you somewhere unexpected, the lobby shows how many players are on each map, and the scoreboards track stars, coins, deaths and eliminations. You can mute other players, and keys can be remapped. Unlike sm64coopdx, where one player hosts the session, matches run on a central server, which is what makes play over the internet work. Mario, Luigi, Toad, Wario, Yoshi, Donkey Kong and Bowser Jr. are playable. Voice and video chat are optional: the camera and audio use direct WebRTC connections between players, the camera only switches on when someone is there to see it, and text players can press T to chat. There is also a machine gun mod, a shooter mode Sauter added himself with WASD movement and mouse shooting, and a slide race track about five times longer than before.

title: MU Online
author: myverya.com
description: Mu Veyra is a browser-based server for MU Online Season 4, Webzen's 2001 fantasy MMORPG. It runs the full 3D client directly in the browser on WebGPU with nothing to install, and one account works across devices; the site says it also runs on tablets and phones. There are six classes, each with up to three evolutions, and everyone plays on one shared server. You can form guilds, climb the guild rankings and fight for Loren Castle in Castle Siege, where the guild owner sets taxes and holds the keys to the Land of Trials. Parties of five earn extra experience, bosses and golden monsters drop jewels, live events run on a schedule, and Happy Hour adds a x1.5 experience multiplier. Experience comes fast at first and slows near the top; at level 400 you can type /reset to start climbing again, and the rankings sort by resets, with a Hall of Fame for the strongest heroes. Playing is free and needs an account on the site. A seasonal pass with daily and weekly missions unlocks 30 reward tiers, including jewels, Zen, tickets, VIP time and an exclusive title; the free track is open to everyone, and an optional premium track adds more rewards for $7.99.

title: Windows 98
author: berrry.app
description: Wine-Assembly is a Windows 98 emulator that runs real, unmodified .exe files in a browser tab. Its desktop launches 3D Pinball Space Cadet, SkiFree, Solitaire, FreeCell, Minesweeper, Notepad, Paint, Calculator, Winamp, the Windows Entertainment Pack, DirectDraw and Direct3D games, and 16-bit Windows 3.1 programs. There is no operating-system image and no source port. An x86 interpreter and a reimplementation of the Win32 API are written directly in WebAssembly Text, and the guest program's machine code runs on them. Nothing is installed and nothing leaves your browser; a program's settings and scores stay in the browser's local storage. Double-click an icon on the desktop to launch a program. The desktop lists more than 40 of them: accessories like Notepad, Paint, WordPad and RegEdit, the Entertainment Pack and Plus! 98 games, SkiFree, DX-Ball and Winamp, and demos such as Diablo, StarCraft, Heroes of Might and Magic II, Quake II and SimCity 2000. Each program downloads its files from the site the first time you open it, and some of the demos only partly work: StarCraft, for example, still stops at its title screen. On a phone, one tap opens a program, and games that need keys get on-screen controls. The project began on 26 March 2026 as a single file with a threaded-code dispatcher. It went public under the MIT license in May 2026, and by early September it had about 3,700 commits, a Win32 layer with roughly 3,300 API handlers, a software GDI, DirectX support, a 16-bit loader and a virtual LAN that lets two browser tabs play Hearts together. It was built largely with AI coding agents, Claude Code and Codex, and the maintainer's design notes describe how.

title: Counter-Strike
author: play-cs
description: Play-CS is a browser version of Counter-Strike 1.6, Valve's 2000 tactical first-person shooter, that you play online with nothing to download. It is a Russian community project with no apparent connection to Valve, and the site runs a short browser check before the game loads. Servers are spread across several regions. The server list offers the classic bomb defusal and hostage rescue as well as custom modes such as gun game, deathmatch, hide and seek, surf, bunny hop, AWP-only, Death Run and free-for-all, plus a training mode. You can play with friends or with bots, pick a duel mode, or rent a private server. You can play as a guest or sign in to keep your progress. The FAQ says it is free, and that paid services may be added later without giving anyone an in-game advantage. The Ctrl key only works correctly in full screen, so otherwise use C to crouch, and some keys can be changed in the settings. Chrome or Chromium is recommended for the best performance.

title: Halo: Combat Evolved
author: OpenCE Team
