No se confirmó ni se inició partida.", "rendered_game_scene": false, "requirements_conflict": false, "observed_on": "2026-11-15", "method": "existing_chrome_windows_ui", "physical_controller_tested": false}
description: Open Halo CE is a browser version of Halo: Combat Evolved from the OpenCE Team. By its own description it is a non-commercial, open source project based on the Halo 1 decompilation project, which reconstructs the code of the Xbox version of the game so that it can run natively on modern systems. That makes it a recompilation rather than an emulator or a reimplementation. Before you play, the site asks you to certify that you own a copy of the original game, and it does not provide Halo's game data. The OpenCE project behind it also ports the same decompilation to Windows, Linux and Android, where you supply a disc image of the Xbox game that you made yourself, and its network games support up to 128 players through invite links. You can play with a keyboard, a gamepad or touch controls. A different browser build of the same game, by Mitchell Hynes, is also listed on this site.

title: Fire Fight
author: Maciej Miąsik
description: Fire Fight is a top-down shooter made in 1996 by Chaos Works of Kraków, Poland, and published by Electronic Arts and Epic MegaGames. It was Electronic Arts' first Polish game. You fly an armed ship over pre-rendered worlds, from jungles and ice fields to industrial wastelands and space stations, across 18 missions on the planets Darius, Jarventia and Ch'ok against the Phantom Council. Objectives go beyond shooting: destroying communication centres, collecting containers, capturing enemies and finding secret places. You have six weapons, from the vulcan and swarmers to the plasma gun, missiles, cannon and grenades, plus items such as shield restores, a cloaking device and mines, with spoken radio dialogue and a CD soundtrack. This port was written by Maciej Miąsik, a Chaos Works co-founder who is credited on the original as an engine programmer and sound editor. It runs the original 1996 code with as few changes as possible, compiled to WebAssembly, and the attract-mode demos recorded in 1996 replay in sync as a check against the original. It was written with the help of Claude Code under his direction. The first visit downloads about 50 MB, the soundtrack loads in the background, and your settings and pilots are saved in the browser. Controls: arrow keys or WASD to move and turn, Z and X to strafe, Space to fire the main weapon and Ctrl the secondary, Shift for turbo, 1 to 6 to pick a weapon, F1 for help, F2 for the current objective and Esc for the menu. The mouse also works: the right button flies toward the pointer and the left button fires. The original game has no license and is shared for game preservation; the port's author says it will be removed if a rights holder asks. Network games for up to four players are part of the original, but in this version they need a relay server and there is no public one yet.

title: Red Alert 2
author: Chrono Divide
file_requirement_review: {"title": "Red Alert 2", "detail_url": "https://ported2browser.com/ports/01M4E03JWP4R4WMADBACBQZ3VP", "direct_url": "https://game.chronodivide.com/", "basis": "directory_about_review", "required": true, "optional": false, "disc_image": false, "scope": "required_to_play", "note": "Importar los archivos originales de Red Alert 2 en el primer inicio."}
description: Note: a Discord login is required to play online matches, and no single-player campaign content is included. Chrono Divide is a fan-made recreation of Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2 that runs in the browser with nothing to install. It is an independent implementation written in TypeScript, and its stated goal is to reach feature parity with the original game's engine. It is a non-profit fan project with no affiliation with Electronic Arts, and you import your own copy of the original Red Alert 2 game files the first time you play. You can play online matches against other people on any device with a browser, using the original multiplayer maps, a ladder with ranked and unranked queues, and Quick Match modes. Replays can be watched, hotkeys are customizable, you can choose between the classic left-click and a modern right-click control scheme, and many Red Alert 2 mods work with little or no change. Computer-controlled bots can be added to games. The project began as an experiment to show that a full real-time strategy game could run in a browser. A multiplayer-only alpha was announced in March 2021 and it has been updated ever since: support for the original game files arrived in 2021, superweapons and naval warfare in 2022, mod support and the first ranked ladder in 2023, a new server and the party-based Quick Match modes in 2024 and 2025, and Discord-based accounts in 2026. It drew wide press coverage in late 2025 and is still labelled a beta.

title: ZQuest Classic
author: Connor Clark
description: ZQuest Classic is the open-source successor to Zelda Classic, a game engine for making and playing classic top-down adventures in the style of the original Legend of Zelda and A Link to the Past. This browser version lets you pick from hundreds of fan-made quests and play them without installing anything, and the same engine is what quest makers use to build their own. The main Play link opens the player's start screen, not a particular quest: choose Quest List there to pick one and start playing. Five favorites are featured below, The Hero of Dreams, Isle of Rebirth, Lost Isle, Link to the Heavens and Rite of the Storm, each with a short introduction and a link that opens it directly. The browser version is experimental, so expect the occasional sound hiccup and other bugs, and it plays best with a gamepad. The default keyboard controls are Z and X for the A and B buttons, Q and W for L and R, Enter for Start and Space for the map; all of them can be changed in the settings. Saves are kept in your browser under the save file name you choose.

title: Taipei Rush
author: aicodewithme
description: Taipei Rush (臺北狂飆) is a free open-world game set in Taipei that you play in your browser. Ride a scooter through busy streets of shops, neon signs and traffic, from Ximending to the night markets and Taipei 101. It is not a port of an existing game: Taipei Rush is an AI-generated game made by aicodewithme. You explore on foot or by scooter and follow missions around town, such as tailing a local named Ming, and the city appears by day, at dusk, at night and in the rain. Controls: walk with W, A, S and D while moving the mouse to look around, hold Shift to sprint and press Space to jump. It also works with a controller, and on phones and tablets with touch controls.

title: Crash Bash
author: CrashBashApp
description: Crash Bash Online is an unofficial browser port of the 2000 PlayStation party game. Play solo or share a room with 2–4 people; CPU players fill the other seats. Twenty-eight arenas are live and free to play, four in each of Crate Crush, Polar Push, Pogo Pandemonium, Ballistix, Tank Wars, Crash Dash and Medieval Mayhem. Choose Solo vs CPU or a battle for 2–4 humans, then a fighter. A public battle opens for four players, and a private battle lets you pick 2–4 and share a code; the host sets the arena, the difficulty and the number of trophies to win (2–7, default 3). The page notes that rooms are Europe-first. Controls: move with the arrow keys, WASD or a controller, jump with Space, attack with X, pick up or throw with Z and taunt with C. In Ballistix, hold Q or E (L1 or R1 on a controller) to slide faster, and press F for fullscreen. On phones and tablets an on-screen deck provides a stick and four PlayStation buttons.

title: Pro Evolution Soccer 6
author: OptiProjects
description: PES 6 is back, and you can play it straight from your browser. This is a recompilation of the PSP version of Pro Evolution Soccer 6, rebuilt to run on the web and super-improved with modern features: 60 FPS, L2 and R2 buttons, more than 100 additional teams, touch controls for mobile, local multiplayer and easy online matches through rooms. To play online, open the game's Wireless menu, create a name and pick a room in the Online tab. Saves and option files can be imported from the Saves tab, and a modern browser with WebGL2 is needed. The project is still being updated.

title: Black Ops Zombies
author: MisaDev
description: This is a work in progress by MisaDev. There is no multiplayer yet, and you should expect glitches. Black Ops Zombies is a browser port of the Zombies mode from Call of Duty: Black Ops (Treyarch, 2010), in which you survive wave after wave of the undead, earning points to buy weapons and open up new areas. The port's page lists ten maps: Kino der Toten, Five, Der Riese, Nacht der Untoten, Verrückt, Shi No Numa, Ascension, Call of the Dead, Shangri-La and Moon.

title: Indiana Jones (Series)
author: BestOldGames.net
description: Two classic LucasArts adventures starring Indiana Jones: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade (1989) and Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis (1992). These are the original DOS games, run in your browser through BestOldGames.net's emulation. The site suggests CTRL + F11 to run a game slower and CTRL + F12 to run it faster, and notes that emulating DOS can use a lot of processor power.

title: Monkey Island (Series)
author: BestOldGames.net
description: Two classic pirate adventures starring Guybrush Threepwood, the mighty pirate-in-training: The Secret of Monkey Island (1990) and Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge (1991). These are the original DOS games, run in your browser through BestOldGames.net's emulation. The site suggests CTRL + F11 to run a game slower and CTRL + F12 to run it faster, and notes that emulating DOS can use a lot of processor power.

title: Toasterball
author: dasher
description: Toasterball, from Les Crafteurs, is a multiplayer physics-based sports game in which toasters are the athletes. Press one of the two buttons on your toaster and release it: the longer you hold, the higher you fly, and each ejection also makes you jump, so you can hop around the field and push your opponent into tight spots while knocking the ball toward the goal. After every goal a random gameplay variant is picked, such as new ball physics, lava pits, portals or moving platforms. This browser build was ported by dasher and is hosted on wasm.rip. It supports the keyboard and controllers; the original game supports up to four players locally.

title: The Lost Vikings
author: dos.zone
description: The Lost Vikings, from Silicon & Synapse, is a puzzle platformer in which three Vikings, Erik the Swift, Baleog the Fierce and Olaf the Stout, are abducted by an alien and must find their way home. You control all three and switch between them, using each one's skills to get past obstacles and reach the exit of every level. This DOS version runs in your browser through DOS Zone.

title: The Oregon Trail
author: dos.zone
description: The Oregon Trail Deluxe, from MECC, is the classic educational game about the long wagon journey west. You choose a profession, buy supplies, hunt for food, ford rivers and look after your party's health as you travel the trail and face disease and hardship along the way. This DOS version runs in your browser through DOS Zone.

title: Hexen II
author: dos.zone
description: Hexen II, from Raven Software, is a dark fantasy first-person shooter set in a medieval world torn apart by warring factions. You pick one of four character classes, each with its own weapons and spells, and explore nonlinear levels full of puzzles and monsters. Default controls: move with W/A/S/D or the arrow keys, aim with the mouse, jump with Space, crouch with C or Ctrl, run with Shift, attack with the left mouse button, use [ and ] to pick an inventory item, Enter to use it, and Tab for the full inventory. This browser version runs on the modern FTEQW engine and is hosted on DOS Zone.

title: OpenTTD
author: dos.zone
description: OpenTTD, short for Open Transport Tycoon Deluxe, is an open-source remake of the classic Transport Tycoon Deluxe. It is a real-time economic strategy game in which you manage a transport company and try to maximize profit by carrying passengers and cargo by road, rail, monorail, water and air. This browser version is hosted on DOS Zone and includes AI opponents. DOS Zone also runs multiplayer servers where you can play with others online.

title: Road Rash
author: dos.zone
description: Road Rash is a high-octane racing-combat game: race motorcycles along busy highways and fight your rivals as hard as you ride, swinging chains and clubs or kicking them off their bikes, and upgrade your ride between races. This is the 1990s PC version, developed by Monkey Do Productions for Electronic Arts, and it runs in your browser through DOS Zone.

title: HoMM2
author: dos.zone
description: Heroes of Might and Magic II: The Succession Wars, from New World Computing, is a turn-based fantasy strategy game. You lead heroes across the map, capture towns and mines, recruit armies, and fight tactical battles in a war over the throne of Enroth. This DOS version runs in your browser through DOS Zone.

title: Warcraft II
author: dos.zone
description: Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness, from Blizzard Entertainment, is a real-time strategy game about the war between the human Alliance of Lordaeron and the orcish Horde. You gather gold, lumber and oil, build a base and a fleet, and fight across land, sea and air in campaigns for both sides. This DOS version runs in your browser through DOS Zone.

title: Age of Empires II
author: dos.zone
description: DOS Zone hosts Age of Empires II in its js-dos browser player, with a fullscreen control on the game page. A keyboard and mouse are the practical choice for selecting groups, placing buildings and using hotkeys; expanding the player gives the battlefield and interface more room. Grow a medieval settlement into an empire by gathering food, wood, gold and stone, training armies and advancing through the ages. Balance your economy against military pressure, counter enemy units and tackle historical campaigns, including William Wallace's introductory campaign.

title: 3D Pinball: Space Cadet
author: dos.zone
description: 3D Pinball: Space Cadet, from Cinematronics and Microsoft, is the pinball table that came with Windows for years. Launch the ball, work the flippers and complete missions on a space-themed table full of ramps, targets and bumpers. Controls: left flipper Z or left mouse button, right flipper / or right mouse button, plunger Space, table bumps X (left), . (right) and Up (bottom), and F2 for a new game. This browser version is hosted on DOS Zone and is based on an open-source version of the game.

title: Fate/Stay Night
author: Kent Hagerman
description: Fate/Stay Night, from TYPE-MOON, is a visual novel set in the city of Fuyuki, where magi called Masters summon legendary Servants to fight in the Holy Grail War. Shirou Emiya is pulled into the conflict, and the choices you make lead down one of three routes. This web version was made by Kent Hagerman so that it is simple to find or share a favorite scene without going through the full game: every scene is listed on the page, and the settings let you switch between the Original, PS2 and Vita versions, between English and Japanese, and show or hide mature content. It deals with mature themes, so it is aimed at adult audiences.

title: Fancy Pants (Series)
author: ruffle
description: The Fancy Pants Adventure is Brad Borne's series of Flash platformers starring Fancy Pants Man, a stick figure in bright orange pants who runs, slides and bounces through hand-drawn levels at speed, collecting squiggles along the way. Worlds 1, 2 and 3 are collected here. These builds run the original Flash games through Ruffle and are hosted on truffled.

title: Vampire Survivors
author: zyxify2000
description: Vampire Survivors, from Poncle, is a gothic horror casual game with roguelite elements. Mow down thousands of night creatures and survive until dawn, choosing upgrades as your weapons level up. This browser build was ported by zyxify2000 and is hosted on truffled.

title: Pizza Tower
author: burnedpopcorn
description: Pizza Tower, from Tour De Pizza, is a 2D platformer mainly inspired by Wario Land and Earthworm Jim, with over-the-top hand-drawn animation and music. You race through frantic levels against a clock, chasing a high rank. This is a web port of Pizza Tower 1.1.0, ported by burnedpopcorn and hosted on truffled.

title: Pikuniku
author: bog
description: Pikuniku, from Sectordub, is a puzzle and adventure game set in a colorful world. You control Piku, a small red creature, guiding him through levels and solving puzzles with a lot of rolling and kicking. This Unity WebGL build was ported by bog and is hosted on truffled.

title: OMORI
author: breadbb
description: OMORI, from OMOCAT, is a turn-based surreal horror RPG in which a child traverses mundane, quirky, humorous, mysterious and horrific lands with his friends. It deals with heavy themes, so it is aimed at mature audiences. This HTML build is hosted on truffled.

title: Needy Streamer Overload
author: EDUrocks Group
description: Needy Streamer Overload, from xemono and WSS playground, is a multi-ending adventure game depicting daily life with OMGkawaiiAngel-chan, a young girl with a rather extreme need for approval. It deals with mature themes, including mental illness and self-harm, so it is aimed at mature audiences. This Unity build was ported by EDUrocks Group and is hosted on truffled.

title: Mario Kart 64
author: truffled
description: truffled hosts the US Nintendo 64 version of Mario Kart 64 through EmulatorJS. The emulator provides configurable keyboard and controller bindings, downloadable save states and touch controls on mobile devices. Use its control settings to check your button layout before racing. Race through 16 tracks with Mario and friends, using item boxes, drifting and shortcuts to gain an edge. Grand Prix cups and time trials reward learning each circuit, while Battle mode swaps the finish line for balloon-popping duels.

title: Iron Lung
author: 98Corbins
description: Iron Lung, from David Szymanski, is a short horror game in which you pilot a tiny submarine through an ocean of blood on an alien moon, navigating by map and instruments. This Unity build is hosted on truffled.

title: Hollow Knight
author: Glitch
description: Glitch's Hollow Knight port runs through Unity WebGL on truffled. The launcher downloads and prepares the game files before opening the game, with a loading display to follow its progress. Use a desktop browser: this build explicitly warns that mobile devices are unsupported. Explore the ruined insect kingdom of Hallownest, fighting with your nail and spells while discovering new paths through its caverns and forgotten towns. Movement upgrades open routes you could not reach before, and charms let you tailor your build for exploration or demanding boss fights.

title: Endacopia
author: truffled
description: Endacopia, from Andyl4nd, is a nontraditional point-and-click puzzle adventure that is visually reminiscent of early computer edutainment games, with underlying horrors. You guide a lost child named Mellow through a world governed by unfamiliar rules. This build was made with Adventure Game Studio and is hosted on truffled.

title: Dome Keeper
author: truffled
description: Dome Keeper, from Bippinbits, is a roguelike action mining game. Defend your dome against waves of alien monsters, then use the time between attacks to dig beneath the surface in search of resources that let you upgrade your defenses. This Godot HTML5 build is hosted on truffled.

title: Coffee Talk
author: EDUrocks Group
description: Coffee Talk, from Toge Productions, is a coffee brewing and heart-to-heart talking simulator. Behind the counter of a late-night cafe you listen to the problems of fantasy-inspired modern people, elves, orcs, succubi and more, and help them by brewing the right drink. This Unity build is hosted on truffled.

title: Class of '09
author: breadbb
description: Class of '09, from SBN3, bills itself as the anti-visual novel: instead of playing some guy who is magically able to score with beautiful anime girls, you play the anime girl. It is a satirical visual novel with crude humor and dark themes, so it is aimed at mature audiences. This build was made with Ren'Py, is hosted on truffled, and lets you import and export your saves.

title: Celeste
author: celeste-wasm
description: Celeste, from Extremely OK Games (the creators of TowerFall), is a precision platformer in which you help Madeline climb Celeste Mountain and face her inner demons along the way. Dash, climb and jump through hand-crafted rooms full of spikes, crumbling platforms and secrets. This browser build is CelesteWasm and is hosted on truffled.

title: Buckshot Roulette
author: truffled
description: truffled hosts this Godot browser build of Buckshot Roulette. Its launcher downloads the game in chunks and caches those files in browser storage before starting, so the initial preparation can take time. Keep the page open until the loading indicator finishes. Face a dealer across a table with a shotgun loaded with live and blank shells. Count what remains, decide who to aim at and use items to gain information or control the next turn. Each choice is a wager on the odds and your memory.

title: Baldur's Gate 2
author: truffled
description: Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn is BioWare's sequel to the original role-playing hit, set in the Forgotten Realms. Lead a party of recruitable companions through a branching story full of side quests and moral choices, fighting in pausable real-time combat based on tabletop Dungeons & Dragons rules. This browser build is hosted on truffled.

title: Balatro
author: truffled
description: This truffled build brings Balatro to the browser through love.js, the web runtime for its LÖVE engine. Wait for the download and preparation screens to finish, then use the in-game menus to start a run. Selecting cards and navigating the shop are handled directly in the game window. Build poker hands to beat rising score targets, then spend your winnings on Jokers, card upgrades and booster packs. The real challenge is assembling effects that multiply one another while adapting your deck to the restrictions imposed by Boss Blinds.

title: Animal Crossing
author: Slider
description: Slider is a web port, not an emulator, built on the Animal Crossing decompilation and PC port work of ACreTeam and flyngmt. The port warns that it may corrupt your save data at some point, and that Safari and iOS browsers have a known memory leak, so use a Chromium-based desktop browser or Chrome on Android. Animal Crossing is Nintendo's GameCube life simulation: you move into a small town of animal neighbors and settle in at your own pace, fishing, catching bugs, digging up fossils, writing letters and decorating your home as the real-time clock and calendar tick along.

title: Alien Hominid
author: truffled
description: Alien Hominid is a run-and-gun shooter from The Behemoth: the FBI has taken your spaceship, and you will blow up anything in your path to get it back. It began as a hand-drawn Flash game before reaching consoles in 2004. This browser build runs the original Flash game through Ruffle and is hosted on truffled.

title: A Difficult Game About Climbing
author: truffled
description: This Unity WebGL build of A Difficult Game About Climbing is hosted on truffled. A counter shows the downloaded megabytes before the game starts. Mouse control is central to the climb: you direct the climber's arms and choose where to grip, rather than steering with ordinary walking controls. Haul yourself over rocks, ledges and awkward obstacles on a continuous climb. Momentum and careful hand placement matter, and losing your grip can send you far down the mountain. Learning a reliable route is part of recovering from each fall.

title: 20 Minutes Till Dawn
author: bog & akane
description: An action roguelite shooter from flanne. Pick a hero and a weapon, then hold out until dawn as an ever-growing horde of Lovecraftian monsters closes in, choosing from a variety of upgrades each time you level up. This Unity WebGL build was ported by bog & akane and is hosted on truffled.

title: Dude, Stop
author: dasher
description: Dude, Stop is a comedic point-and-click puzzle game from Team HalfBeard. The developer filled it with gentle, funny puzzles and narrates your progress, only for players to break the game and ignore his rules -- and the game is written as his increasingly wounded reaction. This browser build was ported by dasher and is hosted on wasm.rip. The page includes buttons to export and import your saves.

title: Zoombinis
author: slippedandmissed
description: Tip: press Ctrl+P on the map to open the level selector. A browser build of Logical Journey of the Zoombinis, the 1996 educational puzzle game from TERC and Broderbund. The zbtools project decompiled the game's Windows release back into C++, and here that code runs in your browser as WebAssembly. No game files are needed, and your progress is saved in your browser. Lead the Zoombinis away from Zoombini Isle toward a new home, solving a series of logic puzzles along the way -- crossing cliffs, caves and a pizza-hungry troll's pass -- as the challenges grow harder. The project notes that the decompilation was almost entirely done by Claude and that this port is not yet fully tested, so you may run into bugs. It is an unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by TERC, Broderbund or the game's other creators and publishers.

title: Catan Universe
author: USM / Exozet Games
description: Catan Universe is the official digital version of the CATAN board game, published by USM (Kosmos) and developed by Exozet Games. Settle the island of Catan: place settlements and roads, trade resources with your rivals, and block tiles with the robber until you reach the winning number of victory points. It uses the current official rules of the board game. Play online against friends anywhere in the world or offline against computer opponents, then climb the leaderboards and seasons. Expansions are available too -- Seafarers, Cities & Knights, Special Scenarios, Rise of the Inkas and the two-player Rivals for CATAN. Level up to unlock clothing, hairstyles and accessories for your avatar, or swap it for a pet. One account works across every platform (Android, iOS, Mac, Windows and the browser). The site notes that some features are still limited after a backend platform change, and that the service may be slow during busy periods.

title: Halo: Combat Evolved
author: Mitchell Hynes
file_requirement_review: {"title": "Halo: Combat Evolved", "detail_url": "https://ported2browser.com/ports/01M3WXT98KK6T8QT8V5K3WNT4R", "direct_url": "https://mitchellhynes.com/halo/halo.html", "basis": "directory_about_review", "required": true, "optional": false, "disc_image": true, "scope": "required_to_play", "note": "Imagen ISO propia del disco Xbox de Halo: Combat Evolved."}
description: An independently hosted browser build of the Halo: Combat Evolved decompilation project (a fork of ecumene/web-halo, itself built on the bnunu/halo-1 decompilation of the Xbox build). It runs the real game engine compiled to WebAssembly; nothing about Halo's gameplay is reimplemented or emulated. The port does not include Master Chief's fight on Installation 04 itself: you need your own Xbox disc image (.iso) of Halo: Combat Evolved, which the game asks for on first start and extracts a maps/ folder from. Stock multiplayer maps ship with the site; campaign missions are streamed in chunks from the deployment's own game-data bucket for players who've supplied a copy. Multiplayer works over an invite link: start a private lobby, send the link to up to 127 friends, and the host starts the match once everyone has joined. Audio starts muted. Requires a current desktop browser with WebGL 2, WebAssembly threads, WebRTC and cross-origin isolation support -- Chrome is recommended.

title: The Old King's Crown
author: TheDefinitiveRoflmao
description: A browser adaptation of The Old King's Crown, a card-driven conquest board game for 1-4 players (60-120 minutes). As leader of a faction vying for a vacant throne, you move your Herald to locations to stake claims openly, while also playing cards facedown to regions of the board in secret. Revealed and resolved simultaneously, these clashes reward the winner and build toward the game's goal: influence. Whoever holds the most influence after a set number of rounds wins the crown. Four factions -- the Clans, the Uprising, the Nobility and the Gathering -- offer distinct playstyles and abilities, with followers whose traits can be leveraged across a map stretching from the castle's heights to the dappled light of the necropolis. This is an unlicensed digital adaptation made with the consent of Eerie Idol Games, who publish the original tabletop game designed by Pablo Clark.

title: Gizmoduck
author: Sova Games
description: A fast-paced DuckTales fangame from indie studio Sova Games. The Beagle Boys have broken out of prison and are causing trouble for the citizens of Duckburg; Fenton Crackshell-Cabrera secretly gets hold of the battle suit known as Gizmoduck and stands up to defend the city. Switch freely between Fenton -- for climbing ropes, squeezing through narrow crawlways and swimming -- and the armored Gizmoduck for combat. Find capsules scattered through the 5 levels to upgrade the suit with new weapons and abilities, and work out the right tactics for the boss fight waiting at the end of each one. Built in Godot and under active, frequent post-release updates.

title: LEGO Racers
author: isledecomp
description: Step On It is an ongoing, from-scratch rebuild of the entire LEGO Racers (1999) engine, built on the isledecomp community's decompilation of the original game. It stays faithful to the original -- Build, Circuit Race, Single Race, Versus Race and Time Race modes, the full cast of racers and karts -- while adding restored content that didn't make the original release, new tracks, and mobile support. This is an unofficial fan project unaffiliated with the LEGO Group; all rights to the original game, assets and trademarks remain with their respective owners.

title: Xenosaga Pied Piper
author: CycloneFox
description: Xenosaga Pied Piper is a fan-recreation of the 2004 Japanese mobile-phone spin-off of the same name, built for fans who never had a chance to play the original release and for newcomers to the series. It follows the original story while adding features from the numbered Xenosaga games not present in the source material: visible, dodgeable enemies on the field instead of random encounters, a turn-order/boosting/Special Attack battle system closer to Xenosaga Episode III, Segment Doors, EVS plates and skill trees, plus a fully original soundtrack and character-portrait dialogue in classic or modern display modes. Playable in English, Japanese, German, French or Spanish. This is a non-commercial fan project; Xenosaga and its characters and story are property of Bandai Namco.

title: Magic: The Gathering
author: shandalar.dev
description: A decompilation-based web port of MicroProse's 1997 Magic: The Gathering PC game, better known by the name of its setting, Shandalar. It combines real-time adventure/RPG exploration -- towns, dungeons, random encounters, gold, inventory -- with a full implementation of the Magic: The Gathering card game for its duels, played with decks built or won over the course of the single-player campaign. Duel and tournament modes against the computer are also available outside the campaign. Runs entirely in the browser with no game files to provide; saved games live in this browser's storage, with an option to back them up to a zip file and restore them later.

title: Pokémon Red / Blue MMO
author: Benjamin Crozat
description: A browser reimplementation of Pokemon Red/Blue built from scratch (not an emulator), reworked into a persistent multiplayer world: other players are visible and moving around you in real time, with a message system for chatting with people nearby and a friends list. It tracks 74 achievements, and progress is saved to this browser automatically, with export/import to move a save between devices. Fully playable with keyboard, a gamepad (D-pad or stick to move, face buttons for A/B, Start/Select for the menu), or on-screen touch controls, and every keyboard binding can be remapped. This is an independent fan project, not affiliated with Nintendo, Game Freak or The Pokemon Company.

title: LEGO Island
author: isledecomp
description: A complete, byte-accurate web port of the original 1997 LEGO Island, built on the isledecomp project's full decompilation of the game and its Emscripten/WebAssembly "portable" build. The core game is unchanged from the CD-ROM release: free-roam the island, take on delivery, rescue and racing jobs, and chase down the Brickster after he breaks out of jail. On top of the original game, this web build adds widescreen support, a WebGL renderer with anti-aliasing and higher-res textures, gamepad support with proper button prompts, and optional HD texture/music/voice extras (downloaded on demand, off by default for the largest ones). Progress saves automatically in the browser, offline play can be installed for use without a connection, and there's an experimental shared multiplayer mode for exploring the island with others.

title: 1080° Snowboarding
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Browser-playable Nintendo 64 version hosted on Lemon Web-Games.

title: Adventure Capitalist
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Browser build hosted on Lemon Web-Games, listed by the host as WASM.

title: Conker's Bad Fur Day
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Browser-playable Nintendo 64 version hosted on Lemon Web-Games. Contains mature humor and violence.

title: Need for Speed (Series)
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: This collection links to the PlayStation versions of the first five Need for Speed games on Lemon Web-Games. Each featured game's link opens its own catalogue entry; choose Play Game there to launch it in the browser. The selection runs from The Need for Speed and Need for Speed II through Need for Speed III: Hot Pursuit, Need for Speed: High Stakes and Need for Speed: Porsche Unleashed. These early racers focus on exotic cars and scenic road courses. Across the collection, the series adds police pursuits, higher-stakes competition and a dedicated Porsche lineup.

title: Rayman (Series)
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Collection of four browser-playable Rayman games hosted on Lemon Web-Games.

title: Resident Evil (Series)
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Lemon Web-Games hosts the original PlayStation versions of Resident Evil, Resident Evil 2 and Resident Evil 3: Nemesis. Use the individual links in Featured games to open the matching catalogue entry, then choose Play Game to launch that title in your browser. Each game launches separately. The trilogy moves from the mansion investigation to the outbreak in Raccoon City and Jill Valentine's escape from Nemesis. Fixed camera angles, puzzles, limited ammunition and tight inventory space make deciding when to fight—and what to carry—as important as aiming.

title: TMNT (Series)
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Collection of four browser-playable Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles games hosted on Lemon Web-Games.

title: Phantasmagoria 1 & 2
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Browser-playable collection of Phantasmagoria 1 and 2, hosted on Lemon Web-Games.

title: RollerCoaster Tycoon 1 & 2
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Browser-playable collection of RollerCoaster Tycoon 1 and 2, hosted on Lemon Web-Games.

title: Ogre Battle 64
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Browser-playable version of Ogre Battle 64 for Nintendo 64, hosted on Lemon Web-Games.

title: Paper Mario
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Browser-playable version of the original Nintendo 64 Paper Mario, hosted on Lemon Web-Games.

title: Perfect Dark
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Browser-playable version of Perfect Dark for Nintendo 64, hosted on Lemon Web-Games.

title: Quest 64
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Browser-playable version of Quest 64 for Nintendo 64, hosted on Lemon Web-Games.

title: Streets of Rage (Series)
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Browser-playable collection of the three original Sega Genesis Streets of Rage games, hosted on Lemon Web-Games.

title: Star Wars (Series)
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Collection of browser-playable Star Wars games hosted on Lemon Web-Games.

title: Rocket Soccer Derby
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Browser-playable Rocket Soccer Derby hosted on Lemon Web-Games.

title: Minecraft
author: Lemon Web-Games
description: Lemon Web-Games presents this as a browser adaptation of classic Minecraft Java Edition. The play link opens its Minecraft entry, where Play Game launches the game and Game Guide opens the host's instructions. This listing is for that hosted classic build. Mine blocks, craft tools and turn a randomly generated landscape into your own world. Dig for resources, explore caves and build anything from a first shelter to sprawling constructions, with the freedom to choose your own projects and pace.

title: Raft
author: Ashen Arrow
description: This Raft browser build is hosted on Lemon Web-Games and credited to Ashen Arrow. The play link opens the host's Raft entry: choose Play Game to launch it, or Game Guide for the accompanying instructions. Start on a small raft in an open ocean and use your hook to recover drifting supplies. Craft tools, secure food and drinking water, and expand your floating shelter while a shark threatens its edges. Every piece of salvage helps turn a fragile platform into a home at sea.

title: Kirby Romhacks
author: RetroGames.cc
description: RetroGames.cc hosts browser-playable Kirby ROM hacks and fan translations for the Game Boy and NES games.

title: Castlevania Romhacks
author: KBHGames
description: KBHGames hosts browser-playable Castlevania games and fan-made ROM hacks.

title: Mega Man Romhacks
author: MegaManGames.net
description: MegaManGames.net hosts browser-playable Mega Man games and ROM hacks from the classic and X series.

title: Sonic Romhacks

description: MakerBurns hosts a growing set of RPG Maker 2000 and 2003 games that run straight in the browser through the open-source EasyRPG web player. There is nothing to download or install. The main directory is the Game List on MakerBurns's GitHub Pages, which shows every hosted game and adds new ones automatically. Only RPG Maker 2000 and 2003 games are hosted, and requests can be sent to the address on that page. Some games were removed from the list at their creators' request. description: vgperson translates Japanese freeware games into English and hosts them for free at vgperson.com. This compendium features seven of them that can be played directly in a browser, with no download or account. The full directory has many more games, from horror exploration to RPGs, and each game's own page carries content warnings, download links and save-data notes. Browser versions may load slowly or misbehave under heavy traffic, and browser save data lives in your browser, so back it up from each game's save manager if you care about it. Several of these games contain mature themes; check each game's content severity before playing.

title: YNOproject
author: YNOproject
description: YNOproject (Yume Nikki Online Project) is a compendium of the original Yume Nikki and its fangames, all running in the browser through the open-source EasyRPG player. Pick a door on the hub page, choose a game and start dreaming. No registration is needed, there are no ads, and other players appear in the same dream so you can explore together. Chat, badges and per-game rankings are optional extras for signed-in visitors. Games included (25): Yume Nikki (2004), Yume 2kki, .flow, nostAlgic, Ultra Violet, Dream Genie, Someday, Mikan Muzou, OneShot, Uneven Dream, Deep Dreams, Amillusion, Braingirl, Muma Rope, She Awaits, Oversomnia, Yume Tsushin, If, Unaccomplished, FOG, [COLD], Okuri, Space Funeral, Love You and Scary Nikki. Each game is played from its own page, for example ynoproject.net/yume/ or ynoproject.net/2kki/. The list grows over time, so check the hub for newcomers. Controls: arrow keys to move, Z / Enter to interact, X / Esc for the menu, as in the original RPG Maker games. Touch controls appear on phones and tablets. These are fan works. Yume Nikki is by Kikiyama; every game belongs to its own creators.

title: Daggerfall
author: Lattymoy
file_requirement_review: {"title": "Daggerfall", "detail_url": "https://ported2browser.com/ports/01M3BAB0GB4VKRDPXZA226JGXD", "direct_url": "https://daggerfalljs.dev/", "basis": "directory_about_review", "required": true, "optional": false, "disc_image": false, "scope": "required_to_play", "note": "Carpeta ARENA2 o ZIP con los datos de Daggerfall; la ficha enlaza opciones legales gratuitas."}
description: Daggerfall Enhanced is an open-source reimplementation of The Elder Scrolls II: Daggerfall, translated line by line from Daggerfall Unity's C# and rebuilt on a hand-rolled WebGL2 renderer. It runs from your own copy of the game's data files; nothing is uploaded. How to set it up (first visit only): 1. Get the game files. Daggerfall is free from Steam or GOG, or as Bethesda's DaggerfallGameFiles.zip (all linked on the project page). 2. Open the project page, press Play, and pick your ARENA2 folder. On Steam it is under DF/DAGGER/ARENA2. You can also drop the folder onto the page; on a phone, hand over the zip instead. You will not be asked again. 3. Play. You wake in Privateer's Hold, as everyone does. Touch controls appear on their own on touch devices. Controls: Daggerfall Unity's defaults. WASD and mouse, F6 for the pack, F9 and F11 to quick save and load, Esc for the rest. Everything can be rebound in Settings. Saves live in your browser's storage. The optional desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux) keeps saves as real files, reads ARENA2 straight from disk and works offline. You need a current browser with WebGL2 (Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari). Still in progress: classic and Daggerfall Unity saves cannot be imported yet, and there is no mod support.

It supports keyboard, mouse and gamepad controls, with a save manager for importing and exporting .b files. Progress stays in this browser. Press Esc to release the mouse; the page also provides classic cheat codes. Explore Liberty City as Claude, taking jobs for rival gangs while moving between on-foot action and driving. Story missions, police chases, hidden packages and vehicle side jobs give you plenty to do beyond following the next marker.

Scavenge abandoned industrial moons for scrap to meet the Company's profit quota. Valuable finds tempt you deeper into dark facilities, but hostile creatures, limited carrying capacity and the approaching night turn the trip back to the ship into a dangerous calculation.

title: Counter-Strike
author: crackers
description: This Counter-Strike build opens a launcher called Global Strike on wasm.rip. Choose a server and enter a player name of 4–18 characters before pressing Play. The launcher also has an Options section and lets you add a custom server by address. The port is credited to crackers. Counter-Strike is a tactical team shooter built around short rounds, careful aim and an equipment economy. Work with your team to secure objectives, cover angles and decide when to buy better weapons or save money for the next round.

title: HowToFish
author: NotRexed
description: NotRexed's HowToFish port runs in Unity WebGL on wasm.rip. Its loader shows download progress before starting, and F switches to fullscreen once the game is running. The build is configured to keep save data in this browser, so use the same browser and retain its site data to keep your progress. After a boating accident leaves you stranded, fishing becomes your route home. Catch and sell fish, buy better equipment and weapons, and tackle quests and bosses to reach new islands in this physics-driven fishing adventure.

title: Clustertruck
author: NotRexed
description: NotRexed's Clustertruck port runs through Unity WebGL on wasm.rip. The loading bar tracks the download and startup before the game appears. Press F while the game has focus to switch to fullscreen, giving you more room to judge each jump. Leap across the roofs of speeding trucks without touching the ground. Crashes, shifting vehicles and increasingly elaborate hazards turn each level into a moving obstacle course, where keeping your momentum and picking the right landing spot matter as much as quick reactions.

Plan a route between ledges, scavenge food and put climbing gear to use. Hunger and injuries reduce your stamina, so a careless fall can make the next stretch much harder.

Trombone Champ turns playing the trombone into a comic rhythm challenge. Move the mouse to change pitch and time your notes to the music; you can play freely between the correct notes, so mistakes become part of the performance rather than just a missed button press.

title: Plague Inc.

Spend DNA points on transmission, symptoms and abilities, balancing wider spread against the world's efforts to discover a cure.

Play with a physical keyboard; saves and settings are stored in your browser. Explore Springfield on foot and behind the wheel as Homer, Bart, Lisa, Marge and Apu investigate a string of strange events. The Simpsons: Hit & Run mixes timed driving missions, chases and races with platforming, hidden collector cards, unlockable vehicles and plenty of jokes from the show. Smashing up the neighbourhood draws the police's attention, so getting to the next objective can quickly turn into a getaway.

title: Serial Experiments Lain
author: ad044
description: LainTSX recreates the 1998 PlayStation game Serial Experiments Lain in the browser with translated subtitles. The options menu lets you change subtitle language, rebind keys and export or import saves. Progress autosaves when you open a node or finish viewing one. The 'Authorize User / Load Data' screen is the main menu: press X to proceed. Explore an unsettling story through linked diary entries, counselling recordings and video clips. You piece together Lain's life by browsing files and following connections between them, discovering the narrative in a nonlinear order. The site's guide explains the file types and navigation if the unusual interface leaves you unsure where to start.

title: Sonic the Hedgehog
author: VinMannie & grubbyplaya
description: A hosted WebAssembly build based on the Sonic the Hedgehog 2013 decompilation, listed by the SonicWASMports project.

title: Sonic CD
author: TWS2401
description: TWS2401's hosted RSDK build runs the game in the browser through WebAssembly. Let the initial download finish before starting, then use the game's menus to begin a run or adjust its options. Race across Little Planet to rescue Amy and face Metal Sonic in Sonic CD. Its branching stages hide signs that send Sonic into the past or future when you build up enough speed. Explore the past to destroy robot generators and change a zone's future, or collect the seven Time Stones through the special stages. Finding a clear route for a time jump gives the familiar loops, springs and ring collecting an extra layer of exploration.

title: Super Monkey Ball
author: TwilightPB
description: Monkey Ball Online brings stages from Super Monkey Ball and Super Monkey Ball 2 to the browser, with course play, stage-by-stage practice, online rooms and a local replay library. Use WASD or the arrow keys to tilt, R to restart a stage and N to skip it; controllers are supported too. Multiplayer lets you join public lobbies or create a private room to share with friends. Tilt the stage to roll a monkey inside a ball towards the goal before time runs out. Narrow ledges, moving platforms and steep slopes turn a simple idea into a test of momentum and precision. Collect bananas along the way, but keep your balance: there are plenty of places to fall off.

title: wipEout
author: PhobosLab
description: PhobosLab's wipEout Rewrite brings the original racer to the browser through WebAssembly and WebGL. Choose the full download with music and intro (about 144 MB), or the smaller 11 MB version without them. Arrow keys steer, X accelerates, Z fires, C and V operate the left and right airbrakes, and A changes the view. wipEout is high-speed anti-gravity racing: pilot a hovering craft through twisting futuristic circuits, hit boost pads and collect weapons to disrupt your rivals. Learning when to use each airbrake helps you hold a tight racing line instead of bouncing off the walls.

title: Super Smash Bros. 64
author: Thomas Dimson
file_requirement_review: {"title": "Super Smash Bros. 64", "detail_url": "https://ported2browser.com/ports/01M2R5GXHZ8CAQCRGM83A2NB5C", "direct_url": "https://smash.fun/", "basis": "directory_about_review", "required": true, "optional": false, "disc_image": false, "scope": "required_to_play", "note": "ROM propia de Super Smash Bros. 64 para extraer los recursos localmente."}
description: Smash.fun runs the game through the OpenSmash project and adds community-created fighters. These custom characters use the original roster's animations and movesets, giving familiar matchups a different look. The project requires your own Super Smash Bros. 64 ROM and extracts its game assets locally in your browser. Send opponents flying off the stage in the original Nintendo 64 take on Super Smash Bros. Attacks build up a damage percentage that makes each fighter easier to launch, while jumps, shields and recovery moves keep you in the fight. Items and stage hazards can turn a safe lead into a scramble.

title: Super Mario 64
author: ArkShocer
description: This hosted browser build credits ArkShocer for the port. It brings Mario's free-roaming 3D platforming, long jumps, wall jumps and ground pounds to a browser tab, letting you revisit courses to tackle a different star or search for secrets. Jump through the paintings in Princess Peach's castle to explore the worlds of Super Mario 64. Each course holds several Power Stars earned through different challenges: race up a mountain, hunt for red coins, explore underwater ruins or outsmart a boss. Collecting stars opens more of the castle on the way to the confrontations with Bowser, with 120 stars to find across the original adventure.

title: Tomb Raider
author: XProger
description: This link opens XProger's OpenLara, an open-source recreation of the classic engine with a playable WebGL demo level. It puts the original game's style of tomb exploration in your browser, with no separate game-file upload needed for the hosted demo. Guide Lara Croft through ancient ruins in the original Tomb Raider's mix of exploration, environmental puzzles and precise platforming. Line up running jumps, grab ledges, swim through submerged passages and search for switches and keys, with dangerous wildlife and traps interrupting the treasure hunt. Movement uses the classic turning controls, so judging distance and positioning matters as much as quick reactions.

title: Phantasy Star Online
author: Bottled_Captain
description: Explore Phantasy Star Online through PSO Reborn. The site owner confirmed that this browser version plays without supplying game files.
